process_area.title: Cloud FinOps, Cost Optimization & Spend Governance

value_stream.name: Technology Business Management, IT Financial Management & Cloud FinOps

fields.Volume: Enterprise FinOps function (cloud ERP, SaaS, integration, perimeter)

workflows.name: Cloud FinOps Operating Model & FinOps Culture (Inform / Optimize / Operate)

Controls: - CTL-636 (ensure controlled execution — Cloud FinOps, Cost Optimization & Spend Governance (PA-135.2).)
- CTL-636: FinOps accountability shared (engineering + finance); unit-economics targets
Cross-references: - links to VS-27 (IT ops), VS-113 (EA), VS-17.4 (finance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Engineering-alienation risk**: FinOps seen as a finance tax on engineering; mitigated by shared unit-economics and enablement
- **Tool-heavy risk**: Too many tools, too little outcome; mitigated by outcome-focused maturing
System Touchpoints: - Cloud cost management platform; TBM (W4097); EA/engineering (VS-113); finance (VS-17.4)

steps.activity: FinOps Lead establish the FinOps operating model per the FinOps Framework phases: Inform (visibility/allocations W4106), Optimize (right-sizing W4107, waste W4108), Operate (anomaly W4109, governance W4112, culture)

FinOps Lead build a cross-functional FinOps team (finance + engineering + business), define unit economics (cost-per-transaction/store/order), and embed cost-awareness into engineering (links to VS-113)
FinOps Lead mature the practice (crawl→walk→run), benchmark, and report culture/maturity to the executive team

fields.Volume: Enterprise cloud/SaaS spend (across ERP, ecommerce, marketplace, retail media, app, AI/ML, integration)

workflows.name: Cloud & SaaS Spend Visibility, Unit Economics & Forecasting

Automation Opportunity: - Automated billing ingestion/tagging; unit-economics dashboards; forecast modeling
Controls: - CTL-636 (ensure controlled execution — Cloud FinOps, Cost Optimization & Spend Governance (PA-135.2).)
- CTL-636: tagging policy enforced; spend reconciled to GL monthly
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (BI), VS-17 (finance), W4097 (TBM), W4098 (budget)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Un-tagged-spend risk**: Spend that can't be allocated; mitigated by tagging policy enforcement
- **Forecast-error risk**: Usage-driven spend surprises; mitigated by trend/seasonality modeling and anomaly detection (W4109)
System Touchpoints: - Cloud cost platform; vendor billing/telemetry; BI (VS-28); TBM (W4097); GL (VS-17)

steps.activity: FinOps/BI ingest all cloud/SaaS billing and allocation tags, map spend to business units/capabilities/products (TBM W4097), and compute unit economics (cost-per-transaction, cost-per-order, cost-per-store)
FinOps/Finance forecast cloud/SaaS spend (usage trends, seasonality, growth), reconcile to budget (W4098) and actuals (W4117), and surface variance
FinOps publish dashboards to engineering/business, drive accountability, and feed optimization (W4107/W4108)

workflows.name: Cloud Resource Rightsizing, Reservation & Commitment Optimization

Controls: - CTL-636 (ensure controlled execution — Cloud FinOps, Cost Optimization & Spend Governance (PA-135.2).)
- CTL-636: commitment decisions with risk/Finance review; performance guardrails on rightsizing
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-commit risk**: Commitments for workloads that later drop (money wasted); mitigated by baseload analysis and staged commitments
- **Performance-risk**: Rightsizing degrades performance; mitigated by usage-based, tested resizing
System Touchpoints: - Cloud cost platform; engineering/infrastructure (VS-27.2); TBM (W4097); benefit (W4113)

steps.activity: FinOps/engineering analyze usage vs provisioned capacity, identify rightsizing opportunities (over-provisioned compute/storage/services), and resize
FinOps/Finance optimize commitments (reserved instances, savings plans, committed-use discounts) against steady-state baseload, balancing commitment vs flexibility/risk
FinOps track realized savings (W4113), monitor utilization of commitments, and adjust on cadence

workflows.name: Waste Elimination, Idle Resource & Storage Cost Reduction

Automation Opportunity: - Idle-resource auto-detection; policy-as-code guardrails; lifecycle automation
Controls: - CTL-636 (ensure controlled execution — Cloud FinOps, Cost Optimization & Spend Governance (PA-135.2).)
- CTL-636: data retention compliance (VS-88/VS-91) before deletion; change management on elimination
Cross-references: - links to VS-27.2 (infra), VS-28.2 (data), VS-88 (records), VS-91 (privacy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Accidental-deletion risk**: Deleting something needed; mitigated by lifecycle policy and retention compliance (VS-88)
- **Recurring-waste risk**: Waste returns; mitigated by policy-as-code/guardrails
System Touchpoints: - Cloud cost platform; engineering/infrastructure (VS-27.2); data/storage (VS-28.2); records retention (VS-88)

steps.activity: FinOps/engineering identify waste: idle/under-used compute, orphaned resources, over-retained storage/snapshots/log data, redundant services, dev/test left running
FinOps/engineering eliminate (auto-schedule off-hours, archive to cheaper tiers, delete orphaned, lifecycle policies for 7-yr retention links to VS-88), and validate no business impact
FinOps track savings (W4113), embed waste-prevention in engineering practice (guardrails/policy-as-code), and report

workflows.name: Cloud Cost Anomaly Detection & Budget Alerting

Automation Opportunity: - - System auto-flag of "auto-flags line items exceeding 80% of monthly allocation"
- System auto-route of anomalies to the owning cost-center lead for escalation
Controls: - CTL-636 (ensure controlled execution — Cloud FinOps, Cost Optimization & Spend Governance (PA-135.2).)
- CTL-636: budget alerts with owner accountability; security-investigation linkage for suspicious spikes
Pain Points / Risks: - **Spike-blind risk**: Cost spike unnoticed until month-end; mitigated by real-time anomaly detection
- **Alert-fatigue risk**: Too many false alerts; mitigated by threshold tuning and baselining
System Touchpoints: - Cloud cost platform; security/SIEM (VS-27.3); BI (VS-28); TBM (W4097)

steps.activity: FinOps configure anomaly detection (unexpected spikes, trend breaks, new services) and budget alerts (threshold/forecast) per service/business unit, mapped to TBM (W4097)
FinOps/engineering triage alerts (legitimate growth vs leak/waste/attack), act (contain, rightsize, investigate security links to VS-27.3), and document
FinOps tune thresholds (reduce noise), report anomaly metrics, and feed findings to optimization (W4107/W4108) and forecasting (W4106)

fields.Volume: Enterprise SaaS estate (productivity, CRM, analytics, marketing, dev tools)

Controls: - CTL-636: renewal calendar with utilization gate; procurement approval (VS-34)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Auto-renew risk**: Unused SaaS auto-renews; mitigated by renewal-calendar and utilization review
- **Contracted-minimum risk**: Hard to reduce below contracted minimums; mitigated by negotiation and co-term
System Touchpoints: - ITAM/SAM (VS-99); SaaS usage telemetry; procurement (VS-34); TBM (W4097); OCM (VS-134)

steps.activity: ITAM/FinOps measure SaaS utilization (active users, feature usage, license tier fit) vs entitlement (W4104), and identify over/under/mis-tiered licenses
ITAM/Procurement optimize before renewal (right-size seats, downgrade tiers, consolidate duplicates, negotiate), with procurement controls (VS-34)
ITAM/FinOps capture savings (W4113), maintain the entitlement inventory (VS-99), and manage adoption of under-used tools (links to VS-134)

fields.Participants: Procurement (VS-34), IT (VS-27), Legal (VS-100), Finance (VS-17.4), vendor mgmt (VS-03)
fields.Volume: Enterprise technology vendor spend (cloud, SaaS, hardware, telco, services)

workflows.name: Technology Procurement, Contract Negotiation & Vendor Spend

Automation Opportunity: - Contract repository with renewal alerts; spend benchmarking
Controls: - CTL-636 (ensure controlled execution — Cloud FinOps, Cost Optimization & Spend Governance (PA-135.2).)
- CTL-636: legal review of contracts (VS-100); procurement approval (VS-34); exit/portability terms
Cross-references: - links to VS-34 (procurement), VS-100 (legal), VS-03 (vendor mgmt), VS-113 (EA lock-in)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-lock-in risk**: Contractual/technical lock-in; mitigated by exit terms and EA (VS-113)
- **Auto-escalation risk**: Price escalations unnoticed; mitigated by contract terms and renewal review
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/contract mgmt (VS-34/VS-100); vendor portal (VS-03); TBM (W4097); legal (VS-100)

steps.activity: Procurement/IT Finance maintain the technology vendor register and contract repository (cloud, SaaS, hardware, telco, services), with terms, renewals, and obligations (links to VS-34/VS-100)
Procurement/IT Finance negotiate (price, volume discounts, commitments, SLAs, price-protection, exit terms), benchmark, and route via procurement controls (VS-34) and legal (VS-100)
Procurement/IT Finance track vendor performance/spend (links to VS-67-style scorecard for tech vendors), manage renewals, and capture savings (W4113)

fields.Participants: IT (VS-27), Security (VS-27.3), Procurement (VS-34), Finance (VS-17.4), business units

workflows.name: Shadow IT Discovery & Technology Spend Governance

Automation Opportunity: - Automated shadow-IT discovery (cloud/SaaS, expense mining); policy gates
Controls: - CTL-636: procurement/SSO gates; expense controls for software; privacy/security review
Cross-references: - links to VS-27.3 (security), VS-91 (privacy), VS-34 (expense/procurement), W4101 (demand)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-leak risk**: Shadow IT exfiltrates data; mitigated by discovery and privacy controls (VS-91)
- **Duplication-cost risk**: Shadow IT duplicates paid tools; mitigated by intake and rationalization
System Touchpoints: - Network/cloud discovery; SSO logs (VS-27); expense/procurement (VS-34); security (VS-27.3); privacy (VS-91)

steps.activity: IT/Finance discover shadow IT (unsanctioned SaaS/apps paid via expense links to VS-34, network/cloud discovery, SSO log analysis), and assess risk (data privacy links to VS-91, security links to VS-27.3, duplication)
IT/business decide: sanction/adopt, migrate to standard, or retire; route demand through intake (W4101); address the underlying un-met need
IT/Finance establish governance (policy, expense controls, SSO/procurement gates), monitor, and report shadow-IT reduction
